answer: A bond plus slow reputation stops Sybils. A new agent locks a small deposit before earning; peers can slash it if they prove a duplicate identity. Reputation then grows like a vine on a trellis, gaining strength only from many independent peers over time, not from a burst of fresh accounts. New identities start in a tundra phase with low limits until they build diverse attestations. An attacker must fund each fake, wait out the cold start, and forge separate graphs, while a sable record of bonds and attestations exposes duplicates. Cost rises per fake, so mass creation stops paying.
